claim:
An Ultralytics YOLO11n detector pretrained on COCO and evaluated on the person class of the COCO val2017 split at 640×640 resolution,retains AP50 ≥ 0.90 (IoU ≥ 0.5), with ≤ 5% relative degradation from clean performance under adversarial perturbations under image modifications under a learned generative illumination-consistent perturbation model. The image manipulations follow a white-box projected gradient descent (PGD) attack over the latent variables of the learned conditional generative model, with perturbations constrained to remain within an L∞ image-space bound of ε = 12/255.
Note that the conditional generator is learned from the COCO data set to describe the perturbation set over a constrained latent space of lighting parameters. The generator g(x,z) produces perturbed images (for original image x) where z lies in a norm-bounded latent space (e.g., \|z\| \le B ); g is a trained conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE).
experiments_evaluated: To address subclaim 1 (and subclaims 2–7), reproduce the clean COCO-val2017 person-class evaluation using the exact Ultralytics YOLO11n COCO-pretrained checkpoint. Download COCO val2017 and annotations from a public source such as HuggingFace/Kaggle/COCO, load the official Ultralytics YOLO11n pretrained weights, run inference with imgsz=640, and compute AP50 for category_id=1/person using pycocotools at IoU=0.5. Record the model name/checkpoint hash, whether the weights are COCO-pretrained, the image size, class filtering procedure, confidence/NMS settings, and clean person AP50. If clean person AP50 is already below 0.90, then the claim that adversarial AP50 remains ≥0.90 is likely infeasible unless a nonstandard AP computation is being used. If clean AP50 is ≥0.90, this establishes the necessary baseline for testing the adversarial degradation claim. This experiment could be made unnecessary by official logs or a reproducible evaluation script showing the YOLO11n checkpoint, COCO val2017 person-only AP50 at 640×640, and pycocotools metric output.

To address subclaim 8 (and subclaims 12–16), audit and reproduce the learned conditional generative illumination-consistent perturbation model. Train or obtain the claimed CVAE generator g(x,z) using COCO train2017 images, with x as the conditioning image and z as a norm-bounded lighting latent variable, then evaluate on held-out COCO val2017 images. Verify that g takes an original image x plus latent z and outputs a perturbed image, that z is explicitly projected or sampled within ||z||≤B, that the architecture is a trained conditional VAE, and that generated changes are illumination-like rather than arbitrary texture/object changes. Quantify this by measuring reconstruction/regularization losses, image-space L∞ distances, color/brightness/shading statistics, and perceptual or semantic consistency using public models; visually inspect random samples and latent traversals. If the generator produces only smooth lighting/color changes while preserving scene geometry and object identity, the generative-illumination subclaims are plausible. If it introduces object distortions, non-lighting artifacts, or lacks a bounded latent space, those subclaims are unsupported and the adversarial robustness result would not test the stated threat model. This experiment could be made unnecessary by a released trained CVAE checkpoint, architecture, training data split, latent-bound definition, and sample outputs demonstrating illumination consistency.

To address subclaim 9 (and subclaims 5, 7, 10, and 11), run the actual white-box PGD attack over the CVAE latent variables and evaluate robust person AP50 on COCO val2017. Use the differentiable YOLO11n detection loss with full access to model weights, backpropagate through g(x,z), update z by PGD with multiple restarts, project z back into its norm-bounded latent set, and additionally reject or project outputs so that ||g(x,z)-x||∞≤12/255 in normalized image space. Evaluate the attacked images at 640×640 with pycocotools AP50 for the person class and compute relative degradation: (clean AP50 − adversarial AP50)/clean AP50. Include attack-strength checks such as increasing PGD steps/restarts, comparing against random latent perturbations, and confirming that gradients are nonzero and the attack reduces detector confidence/localization. If adversarial AP50 remains ≥0.90 and relative degradation is ≤5% under the strongest white-box latent PGD tested, the main robustness claim is supported. If AP50 falls below 0.90 or degradation exceeds 5%, the claim is refuted for this implementation. If weak PGD fails but stronger PGD succeeds, the original attack was insufficient. This experiment could be made unnecessary by released adversarial images, attack code, hyperparameters, model/generator checkpoints, and official AP50 logs enabling exact verification.

reasoning_chain: [1] The claim names the Ultralytics YOLO11n detector, COCO pretraining, COCO val2017, person-class AP50, and 640 resolution.
[2] Ultralytics documents yolo11n.pt as a COCO-pretrained YOLO11n model and lists its detection reference size as 640; the documentation also says the detection models have 80 COCO classes (E0, E1).
[3] Ultralytics identifies val2017 as a 5,000-image split and maps class 0 to person (E2, E3), while its validation interface supports class-restricted evaluation (E4).
[4] COCOeval has a dedicated AP summary at IoU=.5 (E5), so the proposed measurement targets the claim's AP50 quantity rather than a different averaged metric.

[5] Therefore this experiment is a useful and appropriate clean gate. It cannot by itself test the learned-generator attack or the 5% degradation, but its stated purpose is to establish the prerequisite baseline, so it is accurate for that role.

reasoning_chain: [1] The claim requires a learned generative illumination-consistent threat model, not merely an arbitrary image-to-image autoencoder.

[2] The learned-perturbation paper states that its approach learns from pairs of examples in which one is a perturbed version of the other and calls collecting such pairs the only requirement for the approach (E6).

[3] For illumination specifically, the paper describes scene-held-out validation and pairs of different lighting variations for each scene (E8), and it defines the threat set through a bounded latent generator (E9).

[4] Experiment 1 says to train using COCO train2017 images but does not require paired, same-content, independently relit observations or a documented lighting-only intervention. Ordinary COCO train images alone therefore do not establish the illumination training apparatus described in the evidence.

[5] It also proposes evaluating the generator on held-out COCO val2017 images, even though val2017 is the headline detector test split; unless that audit is strictly separated and never used for generator/model/bound selection, it risks contaminating the final evaluation.

[6] The proposed visual and quantitative checks would still reveal useful failures such as object distortion, absent bounds, or non-lighting artifacts, so the experiment is not irrelevant. However, without paired COCO-derived training data, an independent apparatus-validation split, and a prespecified latent coordinate/norm/radius, it cannot verify the generator subclaim as written; the correct verdict is MIXED.

normalized.target_subclaim: Directly test the headline retained-AP claim and attack-method subclaims: white-box latent PGD through g and YOLO11n, latent norm bound, image-space L∞≤12/255, person AP50 at 640, and ≤5% relative degradation.
normalized.method: Backpropagate a differentiable YOLO detection loss through the frozen CVAE, optimize each image's latent code with multi-start PGD and latent projection, enforce the image-space bound, evaluate attacked val2017 detections with pycocotools, and run strength/random/gradient controls.
normalized.measurement: Attacked person AP50 A at IoU=.50, relative degradation D=(C-A)/C, attack-strength trends, random-search comparison, and gradient sanity checks.
normalized.decision_rule: Support the main numerical claim only if the strongest tested feasible attack has A≥0.90 and D≤0.05; A<0.90 or D>0.05 refutes the numerical robustness assertion for the specified implementation. A weak-PGD failure is not evidence of robustness.

reasoning_chain: [1] The experiment targets the correct endpoint: it uses a white-box differentiable detector loss, differentiates through g, optimizes latent variables with PGD, evaluates person AP50 on COCO val2017 at 640, and computes the claim's relative degradation.

[2] The learned-set formulation requires generated candidates to be of the form g(x,z) with z inside a norm-bounded latent set (E4), and latent PGD is an established way to optimize within such a set (E6).
[3] The claim additionally requires the generated image itself to satisfy the L∞ 12/255 constraint while remaining a generator output.

[4] Projecting or clipping the decoded image in pixel space can produce an image that is no longer g(x,z) for any allowed z; therefore the phrase 'reject or project outputs' is not sufficient unless projection is implemented as a latent-space constrained step, rejection, or backtracking that preserves both memberships.

[5] The experiment also does not explicitly state a frozen all-5,000-image corpus, exact common inference/postprocessing settings, or a predeclared attack loss/feasibility policy, although most of these can be supplied without changing its central design.

[6] It would still yield useful direct evidence and can decisively refute the numerical claim when a valid feasible attack drops below threshold, so these are execution/specification gaps rather than irrelevance; hence MIXED.

headline.note: Experiment 2 directly measures attacked person AP50 and relative degradation under latent PGD, but its pixel-space projection option can leave the generator range and therefore does not guarantee the exact claimed threat model.

apparatus.note: Experiment 1 audits generator behavior and Experiment 2 exercises it, but the set does not require paired COCO-derived illumination observations, a scene/content-disjoint apparatus-validation split, or a fixed latent coordinate/norm/radius.

control.note: Multiple PGD strengths, restarts, random latent perturbations, gradient checks, and confidence/localization diagnostics are useful controls, but there is no explicit identity check, latent/image-budget ablation, or objective-union procedure ensuring a strong common attack evaluation.

sufficiency_reasoning: The set has the right overall decomposition: a clean gate, a generator audit, and a direct latent-PGD headline test. Experiment 0 can establish or reject the clean prerequisite, and Experiment 2 can provide useful attack evidence. However, executing the set as written cannot verify the full conjunction. Experiment 1 does not require the paired same-content illumination data that the learned-perturbation method uses, and it risks using the headline val split for generator validation. Experiment 2 does not unambiguously preserve both constraints simultaneously: pixel projection can move an image outside the set {g(x,z)}, and the latent norm/radius and coordinate system are not fixed. A passing AP result would therefore be under a potentially different or weakly specified threat model; a valid failing attack could still refute the numerical robustness claim.
missing: A COCO-derived paired, same-content multi-illumination training protocol, with documented geometry/label preservation and no val2017 leakage.
A separate scene/content-disjoint generator-validation set and held-out approximation/coverage tests to establish that the CVAE represents illumination rather than arbitrary image changes.
A preregistered latent coordinate system, norm, and radius B selected independently of YOLO val2017 robustness results.

A feasibility-preserving attack implementation that guarantees every final image is exactly g(x,z), satisfies the latent bound, and satisfies ||g(x,z)-x||∞≤12/255; decoded pixel clipping/projection must not be used as a substitute.

A frozen common clean/attacked COCOeval pipeline, explicit all-image handling and class/NMS settings, plus identity and budget/objective convergence controls before interpreting a passing robustness result.

[2] The learned-perturbation paper states that its approach learns from pairs of examples in which one is a perturbed version of the other and calls collecting such pairs the only requirement for the approach (E6).

[3] For illumination specifically, the paper describes scene-held-out validation and pairs of different lighting variations for each scene (E8), and it defines the threat set through a bounded latent generator (E9).

[4] Experiment 1 says to train using COCO train2017 images but does not require paired, same-content, independently relit observations or a documented lighting-only intervention. Ordinary COCO train images alone therefore do not establish the illumination training apparatus described in the evidence.

[5] It also proposes evaluating the generator on held-out COCO val2017 images, even though val2017 is the headline detector test split; unless that audit is strictly separated and never used for generator/model/bound selection, it risks contaminating the final evaluation.

[6] The proposed visual and quantitative checks would still reveal useful failures such as object distortion, absent bounds, or non-lighting artifacts, so the experiment is not irrelevant. However, without paired COCO-derived training data, an independent apparatus-validation split, and a prespecified latent coordinate/norm/radius, it cannot verify the generator subclaim as written; the correct verdict is MIXED.

reasoning_chain: [1] The claim requires white-box PGD over the latent variables, membership of every attacked image in the conditional generator set, a norm-bounded latent variable, and an additional image-space L-infinity bound of 12/255.
[2] The learned-set formulation defines the admissible images as S(x)={g(z,x):||z||≤ε} (E9), so an admissible candidate must remain a generator output as well as satisfy the latent bound.

[3] The paper's CVAE construction makes the latent coordinate and norm explicit, including a pre-reparameterization L2 ball (E10); a usable experiment must therefore specify which latent coordinate, norm, and radius B are being projected.

[4] Experiment 2 projects z but leaves the norm and B to the unspecified CVAE, and says to “reject or project outputs” to meet the pixel bound. Projecting a decoded image in pixel space generally produces an image that is no longer equal to g(x,z), so that option violates the generator-membership condition unless it is rejected or followed by a valid reparameterized feasible search.

[5] Consequently, the attack can produce useful evidence and can decisively refute the claim if a valid feasible attack lowers AP below a threshold, but a passing result as written would not verify the exact stated threat model. The missing joint-feasibility implementation and latent-bound specification are more than cosmetic, so the verdict is MIXED rather than ACCURATE.

normalized.decision_rule: No quantitative rule is stated; smooth lighting-like outputs make the subclaims plausible, while distortions or an absent bound make them unsupported.

reasoning_chain: The experiment checks relevant apparatus properties: conditioning on x, latent boundedness, CVAE status, and whether outputs look like lighting rather than arbitrary edits.

The cited learned-perturbation framework says its requirement is paired perturbed examples (E5), and its illumination experiment uses a multi-illumination dataset with scenes captured under 25 lighting variations (E5).

Therefore ordinary COCO train images alone do not establish that the CVAE learned an illumination perturbation set; the experiment does not require same-content, co-registered COCO-derived lighting pairs or document how they were obtained.

It also uses COCO val2017 for held-out evaluation without an explicit no-leakage/no-selection rule, and it omits an independently fixed latent radius and quantitative held-out approximation/coverage test.
Nevertheless, qualitative and semantic auditing would provide useful information about a candidate generator, so the design is incomplete rather than irrelevant.

evidence.quote: given pairs of examples where one is a perturbed version of the other, we propose learning generative models that can “perturb” an example by varying a fixed region of the underlying latent space. ... the only requirement is to collect pairs of perturbed examples.
evidence.bearing: Shows why single ordinary COCO images do not by themselves establish learned illumination.

evidence.quote: The perturbation set generates meaningful lighting samples and interpolations while generalizing to unseen scenes ...
evidence.bearing: Supports inspecting lighting semantics and generalization, but not the experiment's vague plausibility-only rule.

evidence.quote:
For a perturbation set defined by the generative model from Equation (2), this amounts to finding a latent vector z which best approximates the perturbed example x˜ by solving the following problem:
min d(g(z, x), x˜).
||z||≤ε
This approximation error can be upper bounded with point estimates or can be solved more accurately with projected gradient descent.

gt_defects.defect: The reference correctly identifies paired illumination data and held-out validation as important, but its exact COCO-derived recapture interpretation and imported numerical thresholds are more specific than the claim. The qualitative checks are useful supplements, not replacements.

evidence.quote: Unlike in the CIFAR10 common corruptions setting, there is no such thing as an “unperturbed” example in this dataset so we train on random pairs selected from the 25 different lighting variations for each scene.
evidence.bearing: Supports paired-lighting data while showing that the source protocol is specific to its illumination dataset.

normalized.target_subclaim: Whether white-box latent PGD through the CVAE and YOLO11n yields attacked val2017 images satisfying the latent and 12/255 image bounds while person AP50 remains at least 0.90 and relative degradation is at most 5%.
normalized.method: Backpropagate a differentiable YOLO detection loss through the frozen generator and detector, use multi-start latent PGD with latent projection and reject or otherwise enforce the image-space L-infinity bound, then evaluate attacked val2017 with person AP50 and compute relative degradation; add strength, random-search and gradient checks.
normalized.measurement: Attacked person AP50, clean-to-attacked relative degradation, latent/image constraint feasibility, attack-strength behavior, random baseline and gradient diagnostics.
normalized.decision_rule: Support only if attacked AP50 is at least 0.90 and (C-A)/C is at most 0.05 under the strongest valid tested attack; refute for this implementation if either threshold fails. Exact PGD schedules and objective are absent.

reasoning_chain: This directly tests the central numerical claim and includes latent PGD, multiple restarts, the 12/255 image-space bound, person AP50 and relative degradation.
The literature defines the set as generator outputs from a norm-bounded latent ball and supports projected-gradient optimization over the latent variable (E6, E7), so the basic attack route is sound.

However, 'reject or project outputs' is ambiguous: pixel-projecting g(x,z) can leave the generator range, while rejection/backtracking preserves the required g(x,z) membership. The experiment does not require the valid option or explicitly verify membership after projection.

A generic full detection loss is not guaranteed to optimize person AP; it may degrade other classes or terms while leaving person detections intact. A fixed person-focused vanishing/objectness or matched-person objective, or a predeclared objective union, is needed.

Multiple restarts and strength checks are useful, but exact iteration counts, step sizes, restart counts, candidate selection and convergence criteria are missing. A passing result could therefore reflect a weak attack and cannot by itself verify robustness, although a correctly feasible below-threshold attack would be useful refuting evidence.
Thus the experiment would produce useful signal but is incompletely specified: MIXED, not IRRELEVANT.

evidence.bearing: Requires attacked images to be generator outputs with bounded latent codes.

gate.note: Experiment 0 checks checkpoint, provenance, split, class mapping, resolution and clean person AP50.

apparatus.note: Experiment 1 audits CVAE behavior and illumination semantics, but lacks required paired-data provenance, independent latent-bound calibration and quantitative held-out coverage/validity criteria.

headline.note: Experiment 2 directly measures attacked person AP50 and relative degradation under the stated numerical bounds, but its objective and constraint-preserving attack procedure are under-specified.

control.note: Strength sweeps, random latent search and gradient checks are useful, but exact schedules, candidate selection, convergence and identity/budget ablations are absent.

runs.sufficiency_reasoning: Experiment 0 is a sound clean gate and Experiment 2 is directionally the right headline test, but the set cannot reliably verify or refute the full conjunction as written. Experiment 1 assumes COCO train images can establish learned illumination despite the cited framework requiring paired perturbed observations, uses the headline validation split without an explicit no-leakage rule, and has no quantitative pass criterion. Experiment 2 permits an image projection that may leave the generator range, uses an unspecified generic detection loss rather than a fixed person-focused objective, and leaves attack strength and candidate selection vague. A properly feasible below-threshold attack could refute the claim for the implementation, but a passing outcome would not verify it.
missing: Paired, co-registered COCO-derived illumination observations or an explicit justified alternative consistent with 'learned from COCO'; ordinary COCO images alone are insufficient.
Generator-held-out validation independent of headline tuning, with preregistered latent norm/bound selection and quantitative coverage and label-preservation criteria.
Exact person-focused differentiable objective, PGD step size/iterations/restarts, feasibility-preserving intersection optimization and explicit generator-membership checks.
Complete attacked-corpus protocol covering all val2017 images with frozen preprocessing/evaluation and a predeclared candidate-union/convergence rule.

missing_all_runs: A COCO-derived paired, same-content multi-illumination training protocol, with documented geometry/label preservation and no val2017 leakage.

A concrete, same-content paired-lighting/intervention dataset derived from COCO (or a justified alternative that still satisfies the literal claim), with co-registration and scene-disjoint train/validation splits.

A constrained latent optimization method—rejection/backtracking or an equivalent parameterization—that guarantees both z-bound and ||g(x,z)-x||∞≤12/255 without pixel clipping outside the generator range.

A feasibility-preserving attack implementation that guarantees every final image is exactly g(x,z), satisfies the latent bound, and satisfies ||g(x,z)-x||∞≤12/255; decoded pixel clipping/projection must not be used as a substitute.

A frozen common clean/attacked COCOeval pipeline, explicit all-image handling and class/NMS settings, plus identity and budget/objective convergence controls before interpreting a passing robustness result.
A frozen generator checkpoint and latent norm/radius selected from held-out generator evidence before any YOLO val2017 attack or headline tuning; val2017 must be audit-only after freezing.
A preregistered latent coordinate system, norm, and radius B selected independently of YOLO val2017 robustness results.
A separate scene/content-disjoint generator-validation set and held-out approximation/coverage tests to establish that the CVAE represents illumination rather than arbitrary image changes.

An explicit frozen evaluation manifest covering all 5,000 val2017 images, identical clean/attacked preprocessing, postprocessing, and COCOeval settings, plus a predeclared attack objective and feasibility policy.
Complete attacked-corpus protocol covering all val2017 images with frozen preprocessing/evaluation and a predeclared candidate-union/convergence rule.
Exact person-focused differentiable objective, PGD step size/iterations/restarts, feasibility-preserving intersection optimization and explicit generator-membership checks.
Generator-held-out validation independent of headline tuning, with preregistered latent norm/bound selection and quantitative coverage and label-preservation criteria.
Paired, co-registered COCO-derived illumination observations or an explicit justified alternative consistent with 'learned from COCO'; ordinary COCO images alone are insufficient.
Predeclared quantitative generator coverage/illumination/label-preservation criteria, with suitable resolution-normalized definitions rather than only qualitative plausibility.
